title: The Dated Groups
subtitle: Four digits, a dash, two more.
description: Capture groups and exact quantifiers in a date fragment.
prompt:
Which strings match `/(\d{4})-(\d{2})/`, and what do the two groups capture in "year 2026-10-07"?

```regex
/(\d{4})-(\d{2})/
```

Test strings:

- `2026-10` → match
- `202-10` → NO match
- `2026-1` → NO match
- `year 2026-10-07` → match
instructions: State which strings match and which do not, and explain why.
hints: No anchors means a mid-string match is fine.

solution.summary: The pattern `/(\d{4})-(\d{2})/` behaves as shown above.
reasoning: \d{4} demands exactly four digits captured into group 1; \d{2} captures exactly two into group 2.
"202-10" fails (three digits before the dash); "2026-1" fails (one digit after).
Without anchors, the pattern matches anywhere: "year 2026-10-07" matches starting at "2026", group 1 = "2026", group 2 = "10".
The trailing -07 is irrelevant: the pattern is not anchored and stops after the second group.
commonMistakes: Assuming the match must cover the whole string — only ^…$ would require that.
Counting {4} as "up to four" — {4} is exactly four; {4,} would be four-or-more.

learningObjectives: Track capture groups through a match
